name: 大鷹鵑
illustrationTaxon: Hierococcyx sparverioides adult: grey crown and face, bright yellow orbital ring, brown mantle and upperwing, white underparts with heavy dark-rufous streaking and bars, grey dark-barred tail, yellow feet

similarSpecies.distinction: 八聲杜鵑只有18–23 cm，灰頭、橙腹且體型纖細；大鷹鵑38–40 cm，黃眼圈明顯，白色下體有濃密栗色縱斑。
烏鵑小而纖瘦，通體藍黑、尾微分叉；大鷹鵑較大型並似猛禽，灰頭黃眼圈、褐色上體及白底栗色條斑。

featureNotes: 所有年齡均有明亮黃色眼圈
成鳥胸及頸側有粗深栗色縱斑
上背及上翼呈褐色，羽面有層次

rangeMap.note: Partial broad range context: breeds from Pakistan and the Himalayas east through Myanmar and China, south through Indochina; some populations winter farther south in India, the Greater Sundas, Philippines and Sulawesi. Hong Kong has a common summer-visiting population; green countries are not wholly occupied, and the map is neither exact range geometry nor local occurrence data.

sources.use: Full HKBWS Large Hawk-Cuckoo account read: Category I, common summer visitor in Hong Kong. Adult 38–40 cm, grey crown/head, bright yellow orbital ring, white underparts with heavy dark-rufous streaking on breast/neck sides and rufous-brown lower bars, brown mantle/upperwing, grey dark-barred tail. Adults resemble Crested Goshawk; mostly secretive in canopy. Broad range, HK status and IUCN LC/stable.

Cornell eBird/Merlin account read: hawk-like appearance, long barred tail, brown upperparts and patterned white underparts, orange chest flush in adults; breeds in hill/montane forest, uses lower forests/edges/scrub during movement.
HKBWS Plaintive Cuckoo account read for 0079; smaller, gray/orange comparator.
HKBWS Square-tailed Drongo-Cuckoo account read for 0080; small blue-black comparator.
